scope: One new dev-only adaptive challenger after the original holdout study; not another untouched test
architecture: 24 trainable hourly residual-bias weights on top of fixed pre-gate Chronos; core neural weights are unchanged
update: After a delivery day's actual auction prices are available, update each bias with EWMA(actual minus original Chronos forecast); predict the next day using only prior errors
initial_bias: 24 zeros before first source forecast; no outcomes used to initialize
missing_days: No update without original forecast and complete actual target; decay bias toward zero with elapsed calendar time
decision_boundary: Save adjusted forecast and the pre-update weights before releasing that day's target to the isolated adaptive worker
gpu_policy: No Chronos training or GPU required for this first adaptation test
selection: Single variant, no hyperparameter search; add as a separate prospective challenger only if dev MAE improves by at least 1 percent AND constrained margin after variable costs is not lower than unchanged Chronos on identical days
costs: Reuse existing readiness Battery defaults; same annual fixed-cost scenarios apply to both models and cancel in their comparison
calibration: Keep the existing original 80-percent interval expansion; if promoted shift original intervals by learned bias, label exploratory and do not claim coverage guarantee
forward: Frozen original paper control and policy hashes remain unchanged. If gate passes, seed challenger from dev errors through 2025-10-31 only and then update from genuinely prospective, already-released paper outcomes under this fixed rule. Never use original holdout outcomes or tune on forward scores.
limitations: This tests a lightweight learned calibration layer, not continual LoRA training. Dev results and transferred bias from dev-model checkpoints are not proof of future improvement. Publication-vintage, pretraining and execution limitations remain. No trades or bids.
